sources.locator: Complete 57-page lecture notes; inspected the complete state-space section on PDF pp. 46–48 (printed pp. 45–47), including §4.1 general state-space/HMM structure, its displayed density factorization, linear-state example, AR embedding and filtering boundary.

contents.name: Section 4.1: General state-space/HMM structure, latent Markov state, state-dependent observations and the displayed density factorization
contents.reason: The carrier retains the finite-horizon transition/observation factorization while replacing source density notation by standard-Borel probability kernels and proving the kernel-law construction locally.

contents.name: Section 4.1(i): Linear state-transition and observation equations
contents.reason: The carrier uses the linear equations and adds explicit dimensions, Gaussian laws, PSD covariances and mutual independence, all proved or stated locally.

contents.name: Section 4.1(ii): AR(p) state embedding
contents.reason: This pair does not build an AR or ARMA embedding; its inventory is the general kernel law, the independent linear-Gaussian subclass and two finite law examples.

contents.name: Section 4.1: Filtering goals and the Kalman-filter mention under Gaussian errors
contents.reason: The controlling contract explicitly excludes filtering procedures, posterior recursions and convergence claims; a source overview does not supply those local results.

sources.title: Dewei Wang, STAT 720 Time Series Analysis, Spring 2015 lecture notes
sources.locator: Complete focused Section 9.1, PDF pp. 146–150 (printed pp. 143–147); inspected equations (9.1)–(9.4), the two cross-covariance assumptions, Example 9.1 and the AR/ARMA state-space examples.

contents.name: Section 9.1 equation (9.1): observation equation, dimensions and observation-noise covariance, including degeneracy
contents.reason: The carrier uses the observation equation and permits PSD measurement covariance; it does not infer independence from the source assumptions.

contents.name: Section 9.1 equation (9.2): state-transition equation and process-noise covariance
contents.reason: The carrier uses the transition equation, states all matrix dimensions and supplies the exact Gaussian independent-noise conditions separately.

contents.name: Section 9.1 assumptions (a)–(b): zero cross-covariances for process, observation and initial-state noises
contents.reason: The source establishes only uncorrelatedness in these clauses; the controlling plan assumes mutual independence, which is stated explicitly and used in the local finite-law proof.

contents.name: Example 9.1: local-level model and the need to specify an initial-state law
contents.reason: The assigned B examples instead compare observation kernels and exhibit a singular state covariance with positive innovation covariance; no local-level example is needed.

contents.name: Examples 9.2–9.4: AR, ARMA and AR(p) state-space representations
contents.reason: AR/ARMA embeddings belong to other planned pairs and are not prerequisites for the finite-horizon kernel and Gaussian-law claims here.

contents.name: Equation (9.1) and the note that observation noise covariance may be degenerate
contents.reason: The example accepts degenerate covariance and directly calculates a positive innovation covariance without relying on a nonsingular-state assumption.

contents.name: Equations (9.1)–(9.2): transition dynamics and a separate observation equation
contents.reason: The example holds the transition fixed and varies only the observation kernel, then distinguishes the resulting joint laws by their computed covariance.
